key_insight: Treating intelligent image editing as a single, general task lets a unified multimodal model (UMM) be tuned to both understand and generate images without complex multi-task mixing, resolving task conflicts and simplifying training.
problem_solved: Removes reliance on mixed multi-task training and cumbersome multi-stage pipelines that require massive data mixing and balancing tricks and typically produce performance trade-offs across image understanding, generation, and editing.
method: Define a single "intelligent editing" objective that unifies image understanding and image generation/editing supervision.
Recast diverse multimodal tasks into edit-style training examples (e.g., modify, annotate, or regenerate regions) and fine-tune the UMM using this unified editing signal.
Use a consistent instruction/format for edits and a diverse set of editing scenarios so the model learns generalizable editing behaviors instead of task-specific heuristics.
impact: Simplifies model tuning for multimodal systems, reducing engineering complexity and improving generalization across image understanding/generation/editing tasks — enabling practitioners to get broader capabilities with less data-mixing and fewer training hacks.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: traditional multi-task pipeline (many arrows, balancing knobs) vs. Uni-Edit single editing objective pipeline.
Before/after image edit examples showing understanding + generation in one edit (e.g., localized change guided by text).
Schematic illustrating how diverse tasks (QA, captioning, inpainting, style change) are recast as edit operations feeding a unified model.
Radar or bar chart visualizing reduced trade-offs: simultaneous gains in understanding, generation, and editing compared to mixed multi-task baseline.
paper_title: Uni-Edit: Intelligent Editing Is A General Task For Unified Model Tuning
paper_authors: Dian Zheng, Manyuan Zhang, Hongyu Li, Hongbo Liu, Kai Zou
